title: Deadline-aware fanout and priority microbatches for reranker
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Reduce median and tail latencies for the /rerank endpoint under mixed workloads (many short queries + occasional long queries) while keeping per-token cost neutral and preserving output quality.

Background: Current rerank pipeline batches requests into microbatches and uses a global token budget per batch. Under bursty traffic, long-context requests cause head-of-line blocking and inflate p95/p99. Prior tickets have explored parallel scoring and token-windowing, but we still see spikes when a single long request stalls batch progress.

Proposal summary: Implement a deadline-aware fanout that: 1) assigns each incoming rerank request a soft deadline based on SLA and observed queue times, 2) groups requests into priority microbatches (short/low-token requests in high-priority lane, long/high-token requests in low-priority lane), and 3) opportunistically parallelizes scoring across thin shards for low-priority items if the high-priority lane risks missing its deadlines. Additionally, enforce per-request token ceilings with graceful degradation (truncate + heuristic re-weight) and adaptive timeouts that notify clients of partial results when deadlines approach.

Key innovations compared to past work: explicit per-request soft deadlines (not just global timeboxes), fanout hedging to parallel shards only when doing so helps high-priority latency, and a small on-path KV prefetch hint propagated from proxy to scorer to reduce initial cache miss penalty for high-priority items.
plan: Design: finalise deadline calculation (base SLA + queue_estimate + historical latency percentile) and priority mapping rules
Runtime: add priority queueing logic in request router and microbatch scheduler (high/low lanes), implement per-request token cap enforcement and graceful truncation
Parallelization: implement shard fanout controller that spawns speculative shards for low-priority items only when high-priority lane latency degrades
KV hints: surface a small 'prefetch_hint' header from router based on recent KV keys to reduce cold misses on hot prefix reranks
Timeouts: add adaptive soft-timeout path that returns partial ordering with 'incomplete' flag and confidence score
Observability & QA: add per-lane latencies, microbatch sizes, token distribution histograms, and a synthetic load test to validate SLAs
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout by region -> canary -> full, with automatic rollback on >5% error rate or >=30% p99 regression
acceptance_criteria: Median latency for mixed rerank workload decreases by >=15% in us-east-1 canary
p95 and p99 latencies improve by >=10% without increasing 95th-percentile token cost per request by more than 5%
No regressions in ranking quality on canonical evaluation prompts (NDCG within 0.5% of baseline)
Circuit-breaker behavior validated: systems can return partial results with an 'incomplete' flag and safe fallback to default model when fanout fails
Monitoring: dashboards report per-lane latency, microbatch counts, shard fanout events, and KV-prefetch hit rate
